key_claims.claim: Traditional risk models like VaR and Black-Scholes fail to capture tail risks, sudden jumps, and time-varying volatility, leading to underestimation of extreme losses.
key_claims.quote: VaR, for example, is not sub- additive and does not capture tail risks, resulting in underestimation of extreme losses. Black- Scholes is based on the efficiency hypothesis of markets and does not incorporate sudden asset price jumps or time- varying volatility, making it less useful in real- world applications (Tao & Chao, 2023).
key_claims.location: 3.1 Traditional Risk Models and Their Limitations, Page 12

key_claims.claim: Quantum-aided Monte Carlo simulations can dramatically reduce sample requirements and enable faster, more efficient pricing of complex derivatives.
key_claims.quote: For example, quantum- aided Monte Carlo simulations dramatically reduce the number samples needed to generate accurate estimates, thereby allowing faster and more efficient pricing of complex financial derivatives.

key_claims.claim: Quantum cryptography and QKD can provide inherently secure communication channels for financial data, making eavesdropping detectable.
key_claims.quote: QKD allows two parties to share encryption keys with absolute security; any attempt at eavesdropping destroys the quantum state of the key, making such a discovery easily detectable. This feature makes quantum communication inherently secure, thus creating an impenetrable layer of security for sensitive financial data, client information, and high- value transactions.
key_claims.location: 3.3 Quantum Cryptography for Financial Security, Page 13

key_claims.claim: Quantum annealing and QAOA can significantly speed up and improve portfolio optimization under multiple constraints.
key_claims.quote: Quantum computing, using techniques like quantum annealing and the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), enables significantly faster and more precise optimization of intricate portfolios.

key_claims.claim: Quantum algorithms enable real-time dynamic portfolio rebalancing, making portfolios more responsive and shock-proof.
key_claims.quote: Quantum algorithms introduce a revolutionary paradigm by providing real- time dynamic rebalancing using live market data (Shi et al., 2025).
key_claims.location: 4.3 Real- Time Adaptive Portfolio Rebalancing, Page 16

key_claims.claim: Quantum machine learning can identify non-linear patterns and latent variables in financial data, improving forecasts and detection of regime shifts and black swan events.
key_claims.quote: In market prediction, QML models are capable of iden- tifying non- linear patterns and latent variables in vast datasets as well as improving asset price, volatility, and trading volume forecasts. Such capability is particularly important in identifying market mood, regime shift, and predicting black swan events with greater accuracy than traditional models (Komiyama & Suzuki, 2024).
key_claims.location: 5.1 Quantum Machine Learning for Financial Forecasting, Page 17

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing is transitioning from theory to an emerging field with active exploration by major financial institutions.
key_claims.quote: The quantum finance theory is moving from a theoretical model to an emerging field of research and study. As the financial institutions begin to explore solutions enabled by quantum technology, a new era of innovation is beginning
key_claims.location: 1. INTRODUCTION: THE DAWN OF QUANTUM FINANCE, Page 2

key_claims.claim: Hardware maturity, algorithmic complexity, and regulatory gaps are key challenges to realizing quantum finance.
key_claims.quote: Despite challenges— hardware maturity, algorithmic complexity, and regulatory gaps—quantum finance represents more than technological progress as it signals a paradigm shift in how financial markets will be structured, managed, and governed in the quantum era (Kedia et al., 2025).

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing will shift financial strategies from reactive to predictive and ultimately prescriptive approaches.
key_claims.quote: As hardware matures, quantum computing will shift fi- nancial strategies from reactive to predictive and ultimately prescriptive approaches.
key_claims.location: 2.3. Quantum Speed and Complexity Reduction, Page 11

key_claims.claim: Financial institutions must begin future-proofing their infrastructures and investing in quantum-safe solutions.
key_claims.quote: Financial institutions must therefore begin future- proofing their infrastructures and investing in quantum- safe solutions to mitigate the system risks of this revolutionary algorithm (Sabani et al., 2021).

key_claims.claim: Quantum game theory provides richer strategy sets and contributes to a new paradigm for modelling competitive interaction in financial markets.
key_claims.quote: “Quantum game theory, on the other hand, supports richer strategy sets of quantum bits (qubits) so that players can take into account simultaneous strategies in superposed states (Prodan et al., 2021). This contributes immensely to strategic depth and richness, formulating a new paradigm for modelling competitive interaction in financial markets.”

key_claims.claim: Without robust quantum error correction and mature software ecosystems, quantum finance will remain experimental and aspirational.
key_claims.quote: “Equally pressing is the absence of robust quantum error correction, making accurate calculations infeasible at commercial scale (Dri et al., 2023). Until hardware advances deliver stable, noise- immune, and scalable architectures, financial applications of quantum computing will remain experimental, limiting their integration into mission- critical operations.”

key_claims.claim: High implementation costs and uncertain short-term paybacks make it difficult for financial executives to justify quantum investments.
key_claims.quote: “Such financial outlays have doubtful short- term paybacks since most quantum applications remain at proof- of- concept levels. Financial executives find it difficult to justify such investments against short- term share price profitability pressures from shareowners, regulatory pressures, and ongoing digital transformation projects already straining budgets.”

key_claims.claim: Despite high costs, the long-term value of quantum computing in finance is a strong business case due to potential exponential speedups on hard problems.
key_claims.quote: “Nonetheless, long- term value to finance from quantum computing is a strong business case for investment. Quantum technology holds the promise of exponential speedup on hard problems like portfolio optimization, risk modelling, fraud detection, and derivative pricing.”

key_claims.claim: A lack of interdisciplinary competencies and collaboration significantly hinders quantum technology uptake in the financial sector.
key_claims.quote: “The uptake of quantum technology in the financial sector is significantly hindered by the lack of interdisciplinary competencies and formal collaboration between the main players.”
key_claims.location: Page 21, Section 6.3 Knowledge Transfer and Collaboration

key_claims.claim: Quantum algorithms may exacerbate ethical issues such as algorithmic bias, privacy, and lack of explainability in finance.
key_claims.quote: “In addition, ethical issues of algorithmic bias in quantum machine learning algorithms can result in discriminatory or unfair outcomes, and processing sensitive financial information raises significant issues of privacy and data ownership. With more autonomy and opaqueness of quantum algorithms, accountability, explainability, and ethical transparency will become more challenging…”
key_claims.location: Page 22, Section 6.4 Regulatory and Ethical Issues

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing could cause large-scale job displacement and exacerbate inequalities between tech-savvy and less-resourced financial institutions.
key_claims.quote: “Large- scale job displacement, particularly in analytical back- office and financial modelling, is one of the greatest risks. … In addition, uneven quantum technology deployment—where financially able tech- savvy financial institutions would be the only ones in a position to benefit—would further exacerbate financial sector inequalities (Leclerc et al., 2023).”
key_claims.location: Page 22, Section 6.4 Regulatory and Ethical Issues

key_claims.claim: Bridging the knowledge gap between quantum physics and financial analysis is essential to realize the potential of quantum technology in finance.
key_claims.quote: “As quantum computing moves from theoretical to practical applications, the financial sector is faced with an imperative to reskill its professionals. Bridging the knowledge gap between quantum physics and financial analysis is the first step in realizing the revolutionary potential of quantum technology.”
key_claims.location: Page 22–23, Section 6.5 Bridging the Knowledge Gap

key_claims.claim: Hybrid quantum-classical models and quantum-inspired algorithms are likely near-term catalysts for disruption in financial technology.
key_claims.quote: “Parallel to hardware progress, hybrid quantum- classical approaches are bridging today’s limitations with practical solutions. By combining classical processing power with quantum probabilistic strengths, hybrid models enable effective computation of complex financial problems. Quantum- inspired algorithms are already applied in portfolio optimization, fraud detection, and asset pricing. … This trajectory positions hybrid systems as catalysts for the near- term disruption of financial technology.”
key_claims.location: Page 24, Section 7.1 Potential Breakthroughs on the Horizon

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing can revolutionize finance with unprecedented speed, complexity simplification, and advanced problem-solving, making quantum adoption a necessity for competitive survival.
key_claims.quote: “Quantum computing can revolutionize the world of finance with its unprece- dented capabilities in speed, simplification of complexity, and advanced problem- solving. … While we stand at the cusp of such a paradigm shift, the embracing of the quantum future is not an option—it is a com- petitive survival and long- term prosperity necessity.”

maturity_indicators.quote: Grover’s algorithm application comes from LuxProvide, Luxembourg’s high- performance computing center. They have simulated the algorithm’s utility in fraud detection for financial transactions (Khurana & Nene, 2023).
maturity_indicators.location: 2.2.3. Relevance of Grover’s algorithm, Shor’s algorithm in the field of finance, Page 10

maturity_indicators.quote: Initiatives by D- Wave, Goldman Sachs, and IBM demonstrate quantum computing’s potential to enhance allocation efficiency and integrated investment planning (Koc et al., 2025).
maturity_indicators.location: 2.3. Quantum Speed and Complexity Reduction, Page 11

maturity_indicators.quote: Firms like JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs are already testing quantum applications with the intention of creating sophisticated risk engines that can model systemic risks in more integrated ways.
Companies like JPMorgan Chase are launching quantum key distribution pilot projects with IBM and Toshiba to secure inter- bank messaging.
maturity_indicators.location: 3.3 Quantum Cryptography for Financial Security, Page 14

maturity_indicators.quote: Firms like IBM and Fidelity have started venturing into quantum- based adap- tive rebalancing systems that employ quantum- influenced heuristics and machine learning integration.
maturity_indicators.location: 4.3 Real- Time Adaptive Portfolio Rebalancing, Page 16

maturity_indicators.quote: LuxProvide, Luxembourg’s high- performance computing center. They have simulated the algorithm’s utility in fraud detection for financial transactions
maturity_indicators.location: 2.2.3. Relevance of Grover’s algorithm, Shor’s algorithm in the field of finance, Page 10

maturity_indicators.quote: With emerging quantum hardware, Grover’s algorithm is increasingly being considered an executable algorithm for early quantum advantage in financial application (Zhou, Quantum Finance: Exploring the Implications of Quantum Computing on Financial Models, 2025).
“Leading academic institutions and fin- tech research institutions are applying quantum game theoretic models for financial simulations actively.”

“With increasingly available quantum computers, these models will soon be incorporated into strategic planning tools, which will allow firms to respond wiser to competitive forces and regulatory conditions in changing markets (Liu et al., 2025).”
“For instance, JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs have started to investigate quantum computing platforms to optimize derivatives pricing and liquidity planning.”
maturity_indicators.location: Page 19, Section 5.3 Liquidity Management and Derivatives Pricing

maturity_indicators.quote: “Such financial outlays have doubtful short- term paybacks since most quantum applications remain at proof- of- concept levels.”
“Industry leaders such as IBM, Google, and Rigetti are developing processors exceeding 100 qubits, with fault- tolerant systems projected within the decade.”
maturity_indicators.location: Page 24, Section 7.1 Potential Breakthroughs on the Horizon

maturity_indicators.quote: “These are not thought experiments but are being explored by leading institutions in the form of pilot projects, quantum competence centers, and hybrid computing architectures.”

open_questions.question: How does quantum computing distinguish itself from classical computing in solving intricate financial issues such as risk calculation and volatility modelling?
open_questions.quote: •  How does quantum computing distinguish itself from classical computing in the use of solving intricate financial issues, including risk calculation and modelling volatility?

open_questions.question: What are the benefits of quantum computing for portfolio optimization and how might it redefine long-term financial plans?
open_questions.quote: •  What are the benefits of quantum computing for portfolio optimization, and how might it redefine long- term financial plans?

open_questions.question: What technological, institutional, or ethical challenges limit the development of quantum finance, and how can institutions overcome them?
open_questions.quote: •  What are the underlying challenges — technological, institutional, or ethical — to the development of quantum finance, and how can financial institutions strategically surmount them?

open_questions.question: To what extent can quantum approaches transform classical risk assessment practices and manage financial uncertainty differently from classical models?
open_questions.quote: This meets the research purpose of determining the extent to which quantum approaches can transform practices of classical risk assessment and directly answers the research question of how quantum computing is different from classical models in managing financial uncertainty (Irfan, Mohammed, Kassim, & Ofori, 2024).
open_questions.location: 1.3. Purpose and Scope of the Chapter, Page 4-5

open_questions.question: How can hardware advances deliver stable, noise-immune, and scalable architectures necessary for mission-critical financial applications?
open_questions.quote: “Until hardware advances deliver stable, noise- immune, and scalable architectures, financial applications of quantum computing will remain experimental, limiting their integration into mission- critical operations.”

open_questions.question: How will regulators develop general standards and regulatory frameworks for quantum-enabled financial products and high-stakes applications?
open_questions.quote: “Regulators have yet to come up with general standards applicable to quantum- enabled financial products, and there is a gray area for using them in high- stakes applications such as credit scoring, automated trading, and fraud detection. … prompting policymakers to create regulatory frameworks concurrently with technological progress.”
open_questions.location: Page 22, Section 6.4 Regulatory and Ethical Issues

open_questions.question: What inclusive access models and policy frameworks are needed to prevent monopolistic designs and financial sector inequalities in quantum technology deployment?
open_questions.quote: “In addition, uneven quantum technology deployment—where financially able tech- savvy financial institutions would be the only ones in a position to benefit—would further exacerbate financial sector inequalities (Leclerc et al., 2023). This calls for inclusive access models and policy frameworks to prevent mo- nopolistic designs.”
open_questions.location: Page 22, Section 6.4 Regulatory and Ethical Issues

open_questions.question: How can the financial sector effectively reskill professionals and build a pipeline of quantum-proficient talent?
open_questions.quote: “Quantum literacy must be infused into finance education through academic programs, certification, and industry collaborations. Business schools and finance departments must begin integrating quantum computing essentials into curricula, establishing a pipeline of professionals capable of navigating and capitalizing on quantum- driven innovations in risk modelling, asset management, and cryptographic security (Malhotra et al., 2025).”
open_questions.location: Page 22–23, Section 6.5 Bridging the Knowledge Gap

open_questions.question: How should regulators adapt supervisory regimes and establish standards for quantum-resistant cryptography while maintaining compliance with existing frameworks?
open_questions.quote: “Institu- tions must anticipate post- quantum cryptography requirements while continuing to comply with existing frameworks such as GDPR, Basel III, and data localisation mandates (Vaishnavi & Pillai, 2021). Agencies including the SEC, FCA, and RBI will need to adapt supervisory regimes by embedding quantum- sensitive protocols into cybersecurity measures, stress testing, and risk disclosure obligations, ensuring that innovation aligns with market stability.”
open_questions.location: Page 24, Section 7.2 Regulatory and Ethical Considerations

open_questions.question: What coordinated strategies should banks and regulators adopt to prepare for a quantum-powered financial future?
open_questions.quote: “Preparing for a quantum- powered financial future requires coordinated strategies encompassing technological readiness, human capital, and institutional adaptation. … Governments and financial regulators must establish standards for quantum- resistant cryptography to protect distributed systems from emerging threats. Hybrid quantum- classical models provide a pragmatic near- term path, balancing quantum advantages with stability.”
open_questions.location: Page 25, Section 7.3 Preparing for a Quantum Future

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing is a developing technology that can potentially revolutionize the financial services industry.
key_claims.quote: It is required to know about the potential uses of quantum computing in financial services because it is a developing technology that can potentially revolutionize the industry.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing can provide significant competitive advantages in financial modeling, supply chain optimization, and simulation.
key_claims.quote: This brings significant competitive advantages for those willing to leverage its power in areas such as financial modeling, supply chain optimization, and simulation.
key_claims.location: Section 1.1 Why do we want to use quantum computing in finance? / Page 3

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing projects remain a high risk, high reward asset class and must be approached cautiously and strategically.
key_claims.quote: Quantum computing projects remain a high risk, high reward asset class, and therefore it is crucial to be cautious and strategic when considering quantum invest- ment and implementation.
key_claims.location: Section 1.1 Why do we want to use quantum computing in finance? / Page 3

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing in finance is currently in a nascent and exploratory stage.
key_claims.quote: Quantum computing in finance is now in a nascent and exploratory stage with a substantial amount of investment and research (Zafar, 2025).
key_claims.location: Section 1.2 Current State of Quantum Finance Integration / Page 3–4

key_claims.claim: Financial services firms are test-driving early-stage quantum solutions mainly in optimization and security.
key_claims.quote: Financial services firms are now test- driving a small set of early- stage quantum solutions, especially in optimization and security.
key_claims.location: Section 1.2 Current State of Quantum Finance Integration / Page 4

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing can boost human expert judgment and make accounting and finance processes more efficient, leading to more precise conclusions.
key_claims.quote: Banks would be able to utilize quantum computing to boost human expert judge- ment and make accounting and finance processes more efficient. Any conclusions that result from this would be more precise (Chambers- Jones, 2021).
key_claims.location: Section 2. FINANCE APPLICATIONS OF QUANTUM -  COMPUTING / Page 5

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing facilitates critical and automated decision-making in real time in corporate banking.
key_claims.quote: Quantum computing facilitates making critical decisions and even automated decision- making in real- time (Ghosh, 2024).

key_claims.claim: Quantum machine learning can decrease the cost of risk and facilitate more deals with increased profits.
key_claims.quote: Quantum machine learning can enable decision makers to take into account a broader set of variables and assets when it comes to simulating risks (Patel, 2025). It can decrease the cost of risk and facilitate more deals with increased profits.

key_claims.claim: Professionals currently believe quantum computing only marginally enhances rule-based fraud detection, though it can improve precision by using additional variables.
key_claims.quote: Although professionals now believe that quantum computing is only marginally able to enhance rule- based fraud detection, employing additional variables will be able to make fraud- detection algorithms more precise.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing can directly solve the long-term issue of balancing returns and variance in portfolio construction with greater speed and accuracy.
key_claims.quote: This capability will solve directly the long- term issue of striking the balance between returns and variance with greater velocity and greater accuracy.

key_claims.claim: The advantages of quantum computing in retail banking are considered minimal because problems are less complex and contain fewer variables.
key_claims.quote: Because the problems in retail banking are typically less complex and contain fewer variables, most think that the advantages in this segment are minimal.

key_claims.claim: Quantum states are non-falsifiable money and quantum payments could transform the banking system.
key_claims.quote: Quantum states are true non falsifiable money because they cannot be replicated. ... When quantum money is implemented in a stabilized fashion then this will completely transform the banking system.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing in investment banking is not just about speed but provides an extra degree of decision-making by processing huge, complex market variables.
key_claims.quote: Quantum computing investment banking is not merely doing more calculations faster, but it provides the extra degree of decision- making. Quantum computing, which relies on the principles of quantum mechanics, also gives investment banks the capacity to quantify and process huge, complex variables in the market in previously unattainable manners.

key_claims.claim: Quantum Monte Carlo algorithms could rather easily become the norm in conventional pools of models and techniques.
key_claims.quote: in this sense, quantum computing could rather easily become the norm to the conventional pools of models and techniques.

key_claims.claim: QKD has potential to be useful in financial communication networks when organizations want guaranteed security.
key_claims.quote: QKD does have the potential to be useful in a communication network when financial organizations actually want to have a guarantee of security.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computers can perform risk simulations many orders of magnitude faster, resulting in better and more correct risk assessment.
key_claims.quote: Quantum com- puters can readily perform these simulations many orders of magnitude faster, and offer more modelable variables and scenarios. This will result in better and correct risk assessment of the complex derivative and of the interlinked financial system.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing presents both revolutionary possibilities and serious risks for central banking and monetary policy.

problem_domains.description: The paper frames portfolio optimization as requiring analysis of a vast number of asset allocation scenarios, which becomes computationally prohibitive for classical methods as the number of assets grows.
problem_domains.quote: In the results section of this research paper, the proficiency of quantum computing within financial systems as concerning portfolio optimization, risk management, derivative price and Monte Carlo simulation is covered.

problem_domains.description: The need to determine optimal portfolio weights over many assets leads to extremely long computation times with classical algorithms.
problem_domains.quote: In conventional finance systems, portfolio selection has been a paramount question – but one which becomes even computationally prohibitive as the number of assets in the portfolio rises.

problem_domains.problem: Monte Carlo simulations for pricing derivatives and assessing risk
problem_domains.description: Monte Carlo methods for pricing derivatives and risk assessment require many samples and become very costly for complex modern financial products.
problem_domains.quote: The Monte Carlo simulation has become prominently utilized within the financial industry for determining the value of financial derivatives.

problem_domains.description: Pricing derivatives such as options, especially with sensitivities like Vega and for exotic instruments, is computationally intensive and often relies on simplifying assumptions.
problem_domains.quote: Various applications of quantum computing include for instance derivative pricing like the pricing of options.

problem_domains.description: Computing option sensitivities like Vega for large portfolios or complex instruments is costly with classical methods.
problem_domains.quote: Further, estimation of sensitivities like Vega and Gamma, which is valuable in measuring the extent of price fluctuation with respect to volatility and other factors could be relatively costly if one has to compute them on a large portfolio, or with more complex instruments.

problem_domains.problem: risk management and Value at Risk (VaR)
problem_domains.description: Assessing portfolio risk under different conditions using VaR is complex and computationally demanding, especially for large datasets and complex portfolios.
problem_domains.quote: It is important in finance to consider how much one may lose under different conditions hence risk management. The Value at  Risk (VaR) method is widely used for assessing the risk connected to an asset or a portfolio.

problem_domains.problem: simulation of complex financial networks for risk analysis
problem_domains.description: Simulating actual financial networks and multiple risk scenarios is difficult for classical methods when systems are complex.
problem_domains.quote: Risk analysis is a field that also benefits from the new abilities of quantum computing, as it can use quantum walks to simulate actual financial networks.

problem_domains.problem: fraud detection and cybersecurity in financial transactions
problem_domains.description: Detecting fraudulent activities and ensuring cybersecurity is increasingly critical as transaction volumes and speeds grow, and current cryptographic methods are threatened by quantum attacks.
problem_domains.quote: Quantum computing can also make another great shift within the domain of fraud detection as well as cybersecurity [8]. With more and more financial transactions transpiring and the speed of these transactions increasing as well, it is increasingly crucial to keep data safe.

problem_domains.problem: threat to classical cryptography (RSA, elliptic curves) used in finance
problem_domains.description: Widely used encryption methods like RSA and elliptic curves that underpin digital financial security are vulnerable to quantum attacks.
problem_domains.quote:
Traditional encryption techniques including RSA as well as elliptic curves sort the fundamentals for security in the digital domain.  
But these methods could be endangered by quantum attacks, which are based on quantum algorithms such as Shor’s algorithm for factoring large numbers with a high efficiency and, hence, for threatening widespread cryptographic systems  [9].

problem_domains.problem: machine learning and AI for financial forecasting and analytics
problem_domains.description: Existing machine learning models for processing huge amounts of market data and making forecasts are limited by classical computational power and accuracy on large-scale data.
problem_domains.quote:
People use machine learning algorithms in virtually almost every type of financing and investment applications to process huge amounts of market data and make forecasts  
[11]. However, classical computers are already on the way to make such progresses in this field, and if quantum systems can outcompete and surpass the limit of classical computers in computation and accuracy of large-scale data analysis, the new generation of analytical tools may be born.

problem_domains.problem: big data and complex financial models in general
problem_domains.description: The exponential growth of financial data and increasing complexity of financial models strain classical computing capabilities for real-time decision-making.
problem_domains.quote: These are but some of the possibilities that quantum computing can address: the exponential generation of data, the growing complexity of financial models that underlie financial engineering decisions, and the speed or real-time decision-making that characterizes modern finance.

problem_domains.problem: scalability limits of classical computing in finance

key_claims.claim: Quantum algorithms can provide quadratic speedups for financial problems such as portfolio optimization, risk management, derivative pricing, and Monte Carlo simulation.
key_claims.quote: Based on the presented results, it is revealed that there is a possibility of quadratic speed-up for quantum computing based on such properties as superposition and entanglement when solving financial problems.

key_claims.claim: Quantum annealing can find optimal portfolio weights much faster than classical algorithms, especially for large portfolios.
key_claims.quote: Quantum annealing can locate the value of the portfolio weights faster than classical algorithms especially when working with large portfolios with many assets.

key_claims.claim: Quantum Monte Carlo with amplitude estimation achieves higher accuracy with far fewer simulations, making it ideal for pricing derivatives.
key_claims.quote: Compared to other simulations, quantum Monte Carlo simulations can arrive at a higher level of accuracy with far fewer simulations and is, therefore, ideal for pricing other derivative securities like options.

key_claims.claim: Quantum Gradient Descent can accelerate the computation of option sensitivities compared to classical methods.
key_claims.quote: Other quantum algorithms such as Quantum Gradient Descent can accelerate the determination of option sensitivities because they are able to find the gradient of price with respect to input parameters such as volatility and interest rates much faster.

key_claims.claim: Quantum walks can improve Monte Carlo-based risk estimation by evaluating multiple risk scenarios more efficiently than classical computing.
key_claims.quote: Quantum Walks can be used to perform optimization of Monte Carlo simulation more effectively for obtaining better estimation of multiple probable risk situations, which cannot be efficiently estimated using classical computing.

key_claims.claim: Quantum algorithms can detect fraud and anomalies in large financial datasets better and more quickly than classical systems.
key_claims.quote: Also, quantum algorithms could be used in fraud detection systems where it can recognize deviations in big data, including credit card records or trade activities, better and more quickly than classical systems.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing threatens current cryptographic systems such as RSA and elliptic curves, necessitating quantum-resistant encryption.
key_claims.quote: But these methods could be endangered by quantum attacks, which are based on quantum algorithms such as Shor’s algorithm for factoring large numbers with a high efficiency and, hence, for threatening widespread cryptographic systems  [9].

key_claims.claim: Quantum machine learning could surpass classical models in large-scale financial data analysis, enabling a new generation of analytical tools.
key_claims.quote: if quantum systems can outcompete and surpass the limit of classical computers in computation and accuracy of large-scale data analysis, the new generation of analytical tools may be born.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing in finance is still largely experimental, with hardware and algorithmic challenges remaining.
key_claims.quote: Despite still being largely experimental, the use of quantum computing in finance seems to provide some improvements out of the gate, indicating it has the potential to deliver a drastically different paradigm for finance.

key_claims.claim: There is a lack of mature, practical quantum finance algorithms, with much of the research still heuristic.
key_claims.quote: Besides, there is a lack of truly quantum finance algorithms because most of quantum computability research was done without sufficient and often theoretical prior experience and knowledge, leaving around 75% of quantum computing as still heuristic with no practical and more tangible applications.

key_claims.claim: Quantum hardware is currently too limited in qubit count and coherence time for many practical financial applications.
key_claims.quote: Today’s quantum computers have not been scaled up to the extent where they can support a large number of qubits, and keeping these qubits coherent for long enough to perform useful calculation is also an issue.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing can dramatically reduce computation times for portfolio optimization as portfolio size increases.
key_claims.quote: In the table stated above, the effects demonstrated clearly of how quantum computing can enhance the computation time as the size of the portfolio increases in terms of number of assets.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing could offer superior risk-adjusted returns, better diversification, and improved pricing models.
key_claims.quote: The findings of this study indicate that quantum computing could offer superior risk adjusted returns, superior diversification portfolios and improved pricing models by offering more accurate estimates of prices of options as well as sensitivities.

key_claims.claim: Integrating quantum computing into existing financial systems will require new skills, training, and regulatory adaptations.
key_claims.quote:
Banking institutions will have to be in a position to train their employees to get relevant knowledge on how to best approach quantum computing solutions appropriately.  
This may require immigration to internal training and education, In addition to outsourcing from quantum computing companies specialized in offering specialized finance solutions. Also, given the features of quantum computing, there will be the need to develop changed regulation and compliance system in areas such as data protection, fraud detection, and algorithm selling.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing is expected to become an essential practice in future finance as technology advances.
key_claims.quote: Therefore, these results suggest that quantum computing will grow to become an essential practice in the finance of the future as quantum technology advances.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing presents a great opportunity to redesign financial systems by reducing computation time and improving accuracy for key tasks.
key_claims.quote: As this research is going to show, quantum computing presents a great opportunity of redesigning the financial systems. With quantum algorithms, the computation time for portfolio optimization, derivatives pricing, Monte Carlo simulations and risk management can be reduced in half, even with larger numbers; this greatly improves the accuracy of the complex calculations needed in finance.

key_claims.claim: Quantum algorithms provide quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo methods for financial simulations.

metadata.title: Quantum Thinking in Finance: A Toy Model of Risk and Superposition.

problem_domains.description: The paper targets improving portfolio optimization practices, including diversification, risk minimization, and expected return, for investors and investment funds.
problem_domains.quote: we will be discussing how a Hybrid Quantum/Classical algorithm enhanced with Game theory would impact the Finance world, particularly in the Portfolio Optimization Sector.

problem_domains.description: The work encodes a mean-variance portfolio optimization function as a QUBO to decide which assets to select given expected returns, covariance, risk appetite, and budget.
problem_domains.quote: we will be solving a multi-investment level portfolio optimization problem by encoding a mean-variance portfolio optimization function into QUBO( Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization) and solving our problem with QAOA

problem_domains.description: The standard 1‑qubit QUBO formulation only allows a binary invest/not-invest decision, which is considered too simplistic for real-world investment where different levels of investment are needed.
problem_domains.quote: One major limitation of this approach was its simplistic decision model: invest or not invest. In reality, investors and firms never operate in such simplistic binary terms; rather, they operate in different degrees of investment

problem_domains.problem: Need to incorporate covariance and diversification
problem_domains.description: The algorithm must account for covariance between assets to diversify portfolios and reduce concentration risk.
problem_domains.quote: taking into consideration factors such as the covariance between the assets, and the Risks that you may face by investing on them

problem_domains.problem: Incorporating other investors’ behavior and strategic interaction
problem_domains.description: The paper addresses the need to factor in other investors’ and funds’ decisions and opinions, beyond visible data, to reduce risk and anticipate market moves.
problem_domains.quote: These factors are other investors, and firms’ opinions, and future decisions that may cause an asset to go down or up... anticipating other investors can help to reduce risks and potential losses. In these situations, Game theory comes in.
problem_domains.location: 2.6 Mixed Nash Equilibrium Portfolio Optimization Strategy (Page 9)

problem_domains.problem: Gap in traditional portfolio optimization regarding mixed strategies
problem_domains.description: Traditional portfolio optimization rarely uses mixed strategies, leaving a gap in adaptability and critical thinking about other players’ actions.
problem_domains.quote: extending it further into Portfolio Optimization, while not as commonly used in Traditional Portfolio Optimization mixed strategies can, and indeed provide an additional layer of critical thinking, and adaptability to the to the overall strategy
problem_domains.location: 2.6 Mixed Nash Equilibrium Portfolio Optimization Strategy (Page 9)

problem_domains.problem: Need to outperform classical portfolio strategies and major indices
problem_domains.description: The work aims to achieve higher annual expected returns than classical portfolio strategies and benchmark funds like Nasdaq and S&P 500.
problem_domains.quote: capable of generating Higher Annual Expected returns in comparison to current classical models

problem_domains.problem: Balancing expected return and risk (Sharpe ratio)
problem_domains.description: The paper focuses on achieving high expected returns while maintaining a high Sharpe ratio and reducing undesirable risk.
problem_domains.quote: Despite the smaller Expected return in comparison to the other previously stated strategies, the Sharpe Ratio remains above 2 showing the strategies efficiency in reducing the overall unenviable risk while also granting a high Annual Expected return

problem_domains.description: The paper frames portfolio optimization as a financial problem where quantum algorithms could dramatically improve annual expected returns and transform investment practice.
problem_domains.quote: changing the Portfolio Optimization world as we know and eventually causing a revolution across the Finance world similar to other key events in investment history such as The Modern Portfolio Theory.

problem_domains.problem: Annual Expected Returns in investment portfolios
problem_domains.description: The work treats maximizing annual expected returns, compared against benchmarks like NASDAQ-100 and S&P 500, as a central financial performance problem.
problem_domains.quote: despite those same firms achieving an annual return of 118% and 109% over a period of 5 years (Curvo 2025; Marques and Witman 2025) where, this algorithm was able to output similar or even higher results than those firms in a significant amount of randomize choices, despite its limited number of assets and qubits.

problem_domains.description: The paper highlights comparative risk modeling as an important aspect of future quantum finance research, implying a need to better handle and compare portfolio risks.
problem_domains.quote: any future research in regard to the Quantum Finance world should consider  Hybrid Quantum-Classical frameworks, comparative risk modeling, and real-time market responsiveness

solution_approaches.approach: Hybrid Quantum/Classical algorithm enhanced with Game theory
solution_approaches.description: A hybrid algorithm that combines quantum optimization (QAOA) with classical components and game-theoretic mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium to improve portfolio optimization.
solution_approaches.quote: a Hybrid Quantum/Classical algorithm enhanced with Game theory would impact the Finance world, particularly in the Portfolio Optimization Sector.

solution_approaches.approach: QAOA (Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm)
solution_approaches.description: The mean-variance portfolio optimization QUBO is mapped to an Ising Hamiltonian and solved using QAOA as the quantum optimization core.
solution_approaches.quote: solving our problem with QAOA, a Hybrid Quantum/Classical Algorithm.

solution_approaches.approach: QUBO to Ising Hamiltonian translation
solution_approaches.description: The binary mean-variance optimization problem is converted from QUBO form into an Ising Hamiltonian suitable as the cost operator in QAOA.
solution_approaches.quote: in order to solve this optimization problem on a quantum device, our main equation must be converted from QUBO to an Ising Hamiltonian that can be used as the cost operator in QAOA.

solution_approaches.approach: Modified Two-Qubits Approach (multi-level investment encoding)
solution_approaches.description: An extra qubit is added so that each asset is encoded with two qubits, allowing four investment levels (Don’t Invest, Invest Low, Invest Medium, Invest High) instead of a binary decision.
solution_approaches.quote: one of the solutions found was adding an extra qubit, which granted four different investment levels while keeping the simplicity of the algorithm.

solution_approaches.approach: Modified Two-qubits Mean Variance Equation
solution_approaches.description: The mean-variance objective is reformulated to work with two-qubit encoding per asset and a reward system aligned with the four investment levels.
solution_approaches.quote: With the addition of an extra qubit, our mean variance equations, we must undergo some changes in order to be fit for use in the algorithm, mainly changes in the vector notation, and changes in both Expected returns and Covariance Matrices

solution_approaches.approach: Mixed strategy Nash equilibrium for portfolio optimization
solution_approaches.description: A mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium model is integrated to represent strategic interaction between an investor and another investor/hedge fund under Up/Down market states with four investment levels.
solution_approaches.quote: we will be adding a mixed strategy Nash Equilibrium to our Algorithm that makes decisions not only based in the given data by Finance database’s such as Yahoo Finance, but other investors or investment funds

solution_approaches.approach: Application of Mixed Strategies with payoff matrices
solution_approaches.description: The algorithm uses Up and Down payoff matrices and Nashpy to compute mixed-strategy equilibria that yield probability distributions over the four investment levels for each asset.
solution_approaches.quote: The algorithm then proceeds to choose which strategy to use depending on the trend for that asset and applies a mixed strategy Nash equilibrium on the time chosen.

solution_approaches.approach: Hybrid Quantum/Classical Algorithm Structure (nine-step workflow)
solution_approaches.description: A nine-step pipeline including data acquisition, statistical preparation, covariance matrix, mixed strategy setup, quadratic program, reward system, QAOA formulation, and result interpretation.
solution_approaches.quote: The way the algorithm works is by dividing its workflow into nine steps: -Imports -Market Data Acquisition -Statistical data preparation -Covariance Matrix -Mixed Strategy Set-up -Quadratic Program set-up -Rewards System, and QUBO Formulation -QAOA Formulation, and Execution -Result Interpretation

solution_approaches.approach: Use of Qiskit Minimum Eigen Optimizer with simulated quantum backend
solution_approaches.description: QAOA is wrapped in Qiskit’s Minimum Eigen Optimizer and executed on a perfect simulated, noiseless quantum computer to obtain the optimal investment strategy.
solution_approaches.quote: enabling the execution of the algorithm on a perfect Simulated without noise Quantum Computer.

solution_approaches.approach: Integration of classical optimizer COBYLA with QAOA
solution_approaches.description: The QAOA circuit parameters are optimized using the classical COBYLA optimizer with a maximum of 250 iterations.
solution_approaches.quote: As a Hybrid algorithm, an initial classical optimizer, COBYLA (Constrained Optimization by Linear Approximations), is first initialized and configured using a maximum of 250 iterations, allowing its adjustment into the changing parameters of a QAOA circuit.

solution_approaches.approach: Randomized asset selection from multiple industries
solution_approaches.description: The algorithm randomly selects four assets from a pool of 15 stocks across ten industries to ensure diversification and test robustness across different asset combinations.

key_claims.claim: The proposed hybrid quantum/classical algorithm with game theory can generate higher annual expected returns than current classical models.
key_claims.quote: an example of a Hybrid Classical/Quantum QAOA optimization algorithm capable of generating Higher Annual Expected returns in comparison to current classical models

key_claims.claim: The algorithm incorporates covariance and diversification effectively, reducing concentration risk.
key_claims.quote: demonstrating the algorithm’s incorporation of Covariance between its randomly selected choices, adding the diversification needed to reduce concentration risk, a feature central in mean variance optimization.

key_claims.claim: The mixed-strategy game-theoretic component adds adaptability and critical thinking beyond data, hedging against market uncertainty.
key_claims.quote: the strategy fills the gaps by enhancing the algorithm’s critical thinking beyond data.
key_claims.location: 2.6 Mixed Nash Equilibrium Portfolio Optimization Strategy (Page 10)

key_claims.claim: The mixed-strategy distributions are more evenly spread than those of a classical mean-variance optimizer, which tends to concentrate resources.
key_claims.quote: These distributions are more evenly spread compared to a classical mean-variance optimizer, which on average, is known for allocating most of its resources in a few selected strategies.

key_claims.claim: The two-qubit investment encoding yields a more diversified portfolio across multiple investment levels rather than concentration in a single strategy.
key_claims.quote: This results in a diversified portfolio in which each asset is distributed across multiple Investment levels rather than concentrated in a single strategy.

key_claims.claim: Adding an extra qubit increases the pool of investment strategies and leads to higher expected return and higher Sharpe ratio in the long run compared to 1‑qubit strategies.
key_claims.quote: adding an extra qubit, not only grants a higher pull of Investment strategies as shown on the previous Optimal Investment Strategies, but a higher expected return on Investment, and a higher Sharper Ration in the Long run due to the proportional increase in Risk that a 1 qubit Strategy provides

key_claims.claim: The hybrid quantum/classical game theory algorithm can surpass Nasdaq and S&P 500 in average annual expected return over 5 years, despite using fewer assets and qubits.
key_claims.quote: the algorithm was capable of surpassing both Investment Funds with a higher Annual Expected return on average in most randomized asset selections

key_claims.claim: The two-qubit hybrid algorithm maintains a Sharpe ratio above 2, indicating efficient risk reduction with high annual expected return.
key_claims.quote: the Sharpe Ratio remains above 2 showing the strategies efficiency in reducing the overall unenviable risk while also granting a high Annual Expected return

key_claims.claim: One-qubit strategies may sometimes have higher expected return but tend to have lower average Sharpe ratio and increased risk.
key_claims.quote: while the 1-qubit strategies may have had a higher expected return on some occasions due to its simplistic investment strategy it tends to output a lower average Sharpe Ratio across multiple randomize tests... showing its increased risk upon a much simpler approach

key_claims.claim: Quantum computers have the potential to simulate complex economic models and portfolios using large datasets, surpassing classical strategies.
key_claims.quote: Quantum computers would not only enable the simulation of complex economic models (Qiskit Community 2025) using a huge portion of data, but they will also help to reduce risks that come with investing by simulating Portfolios over certain periods of time, not only serving as an improvement to current strategies, but surpassing them with its edge over classical strategies

key_claims.claim: Current quantum computers suffer from limitations such as noise and limited qubits, but a low-noise, fully operational quantum computer could transform portfolio optimization.
key_claims.quote: We also discuss the current limitations and problems that modern Quantum computers endure, and what impact a Quantum computer with less noise and more qubits may have in Industries such as Mutual funds, Hedge Funds, ETF, and more.

key_claims.claim: A perfectly stable theoretical quantum computer would show the full potential of the proposed hybrid quantum/classical game-theoretic approach.
key_claims.quote: As a way to prove and show the possibilities that a Perfectly stable Theoretical Quantum Computer may have, In this paper we will be looking at theoretical at the Hybrid Quantum Classical Computer enhanced with Game theory, that actively shows the full potential of such technology.

key_claims.claim: The quantum algorithm achieved results comparable to or better than major equity benchmarks like NASDAQ-100 and S&P 500 despite using a small number of assets and qubits.
key_claims.quote: despite the small number of asset choices, and qubits, the algorithm was still able to output results comparable or better than modern fund benchmarks such as the NASDAQ-100 and S&P 500 (Curvo 2025; Marques and Witman 2025)

key_claims.claim: The quantum algorithm was able to output similar or even higher annual returns than firms tracking NASDAQ-100 and S&P 500 in many randomized choices.
key_claims.quote: this algorithm was able to output similar or even higher results than those firms in a significant amount of randomize choices, despite its limited number of assets and qubits.

key_claims.claim: Future, less noisy quantum computers with many qubits could produce unprecedented annual expected returns and revolutionize portfolio optimization and finance.
key_claims.quote: in a near future an enhanced less noisy with hundreds or even thousands of qubits, with a higher number of assets would be able to change output Annual Expected Returns never even seen in modern history changing the Portfolio Optimization world as we know and eventually causing a revolution across the Finance world similar to other key events in investment history such as The Modern Portfolio Theory.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computers are set to change the way problems are approached across most modern industries, including finance.
key_claims.quote: quantum computers are set to change the way we approach problems across most of the known modern industries, and as seen in this paper despite the small number of asset choices, and qubits, the algorithm was still able to output results comparable or better than modern fund benchmarks

problem_domains.description: Examines how quantum computing can improve the accuracy and efficiency of financial analysis and forecasting.
problem_domains.quote: The aim of this research is to investigate the effects of quantum computing on financial analysis and forecast accuracy.

problem_domains.problem: large volume of financial data and complexity of financial decision-making
problem_domains.description: Addresses the challenge of handling growing volumes of financial data and increasingly complex financial decisions.
problem_domains.quote: Given the significant increase in the volume of financial data and the complexity  of financial decision -making, the need to use new technologies such as quantum computing is increasingly felt.

solution_approaches.quote: variational quantum eigen solvers (VQEs), quantum approximate optimizations of problems (QAOPs), hybrid quantum machine learning (QML) models, and sampling-based tasks have been speciﬁcally developed to work under NISQ-era hardware limitations [3, 6]; speciﬁcally, they are based on shallow (few gates) circuits, error mitigation techniques, and optimization loops (classical solutions) which keep their use technically possible with only hundreds of noisy qubits at the moment.

solution_approaches.description: The QCSHQD framework conceptualizes quantum computing as a cloud-based complementary resource integrated via abstraction layers and hybrid workflows.
solution_approaches.quote: The Hybrid Classical Quantum integration framework represents a view of Quantum Computing as being integrated into the existing classical ecosystem, while also suggesting that quantum computing will be a cloud-based, complementary computational resource to existing systems through Quantum Computing as a Service for Hybrid Classical Quantum Development (QCSHQD), where the emphasis is on establishing abstraction layers and hybrid workﬂows to reduce barriers to entry through expertise and develop incremental value over time, under the current NISQ limitations.

solution_approaches.description: QFaaS is proposed as an event-driven, modular model of quantum execution integrated into heterogeneous cloud providers and DevOps practices.
solution_approaches.quote: As such, the Quantum Function-as-a-Service (QFaaS) paradigm represents a model of quantum execution as an event-driven and modular architecture that is interchanged and integrated through heterogeneous Cloud-computing providers, while complying with existing DevOps and orchestration best practices.

key_claims.claim: Existing literature reviews focus on algorithms and hardware but do not address organizational readiness, sector-specific implementation pathways, or strategic value creation for quantum computing.

key_claims.claim: Applications like Shor’s algorithm, high-accuracy quantum chemistry simulation, and large-scale QML cannot currently be supported by NISQ hardware because they require millions of logical qubits with full error correction.
key_claims.quote: Alternatively, applications such as Shor’s algorithm (which has a cryptographic signiﬁcance), simulating quantum chemistry with an accuracy of 100%, and large-scale QML require millions of logical qubits with full error correction [11,12]. This means that, based on our synthesis of what’s available, these later types of applications cannot currently be supported by existing or expected NISQ hardware.

key_claims.claim: Quantum readiness is sector-specific and depends on problem structure, digital capability, and willingness to accept experimental uncertainty.
key_claims.quote: Finding 2: quantum readiness is sector speciﬁc and structurally determined There are three observable factors that govern how prepared speciﬁc sectors will be for a transition to quantum computing. These are: (1) The similarity of the problem structure and the types of advantages expected from quantum computing. (2) The ability of the organisation to make digital advancements and have the skills necessary to implement quantum computing; and (3) The willingness of the organisation to willingly accept uncertainty in their experiments.

maturity_indicators.quote: The last decade has seen Quantum Computing grow from mostly theoretical research to a rapidly growing market in both technology and commercial domain.

The current stage of Quantum Computing is known as the NISQ (Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum) stage, which is comprised of Quantum Processors containing anywhere from about 50 physical Qubits up to about 1000 physical Qubits, which have certain limitations due to the high level of restrictions placed upon Quantum Processors by decoherence, gate errors, and limited depth of Quantum Circuits [3,25].

The recent achievements of Google’s Sycamore processor has showcased Quantum Supremacy and the recent advancements in logical qubit stability along with improvements in Quantum Error Correction, as demonstrated by the research of Arute et al. [2] and Acharya et al. [1], conﬁrms considerable progress has been made toward achieving fault-tolerant quantum computing.

From 2004-2012, the scientiﬁc output was comparatively lower than in more recent years, and we attribute this to the developmental stage of quantum computing that was primarily theoretical at this time.
Pure quantum solutions were not found in the real world of business by any of the studies. Instead, pure quantum solutions are virtually non-existent in real-world business applications.

Thus, as organizations look to invest in the near-term future, their investments must be framed as the development of a development capability which generates knowledge, rather than as new applications being ready for implementation.

problem_domains.problem: secure data transmission and vulnerabilities of classical cryptography
problem_domains.description: The chapter frames the need for quantum communication networks around increasing requirements for secure data transmission and the vulnerability of classical cryptographic methods to sophisticated and quantum attacks.
problem_domains.quote: The rise of quantum communication is largely attributed to the increasing need for secure data transmission in an era where classical cryptographic methods are becoming defense-less to sophisticated attacks. On the other hand, quantum communication networks promise to revolutionize how we exchange information by ensuring that data remains conﬁdential and tamper-proof, even in the face of advanced computational threats posed by the advent of quantum computers [ 5].

problem_domains.problem: shortcomings of traditional communication networks regarding security
problem_domains.description: The text highlights that cyberthreats and rising processing power expose security shortcomings in traditional communication networks.
problem_domains.quote: But the advent of cyberthreats and the extremely fast rise in processing power have revealed the shortcomings of traditional communication networks, especially with regard to security.

problem_domains.problem: potential irrelevance of conventional encryption (RSA, AES) under quantum attacks
problem_domains.description: The chapter notes that conventional encryption schemes based on computational hardness may become irrelevant as quantum computers can solve their underlying problems much faster.
problem_domains.quote: Conventional encryption methods, like RSA and AES, depend on speciﬁc mathematical problems’ computational complexity. These issues can be resolved considerably faster with the emergence of quantum computers, potentially making traditional encryption techniques irrelevant [ 38, 39].

problem_domains.problem: need for secure channels in national security, financial transactions, and confidential communications
problem_domains.description: The chapter explicitly identifies national security, financial transactions, and confidential communications as domains requiring secure and safe communication channels immune to classical and quantum attacks.
problem_domains.quote: The primary goal of quantum communication networks is to provide secured and safe communication channels that are immune to both classical and quantum attacks. This is particularly crucial for applications in national security, ﬁnancial transactions, and conﬁdential communications, where data integrity and privacy are paramount [ 26, 27] (Table 1).

problem_domains.description: The chapter frames a problem of achieving reliable, long-distance quantum communication given loss, decoherence, and the impossibility of amplifying quantum states.
problem_domains.quote: Quantum repeaters are crucial components in the quest to establish long-distance quantum communication networks. In classical communication, repeaters simply amplify signals to extend their range. However, the ampliﬁcation of quantum states is impossible due to the no-cloning theorem, which prohibits the creation of identical copies of an arbitrary unknown quantum state.

problem_domains.problem: global-scale secure communication beyond terrestrial limitations
problem_domains.description: The chapter identifies the need to extend secure quantum communication to global scales beyond terrestrial network limits.
problem_domains.quote: Quantum satellites represent a signiﬁcant advancement in the ﬁeld of quantum communication, providing a platform for global-scale quantum key distribution (QKD) and other quantum communication protocols. These satellites extend the reach of quantum networks beyond terrestrial limitations, enabling secure communication across vast geographical areas [31].

problem_domains.problem: synchronization and buffering of quantum information in networks
problem_domains.description: The chapter presents the challenge of synchronizing quantum operations and buffering quantum information across network nodes.
problem_domains.quote: Quantum memory allows for the synchronization of quantum operations and the coordination of entanglement distribution across different network nodes. This synchronization is vital for the successful operation of quantum repeaters and the maintenance of entanglement over long distances. By temporarily storing quantum states, quantum memory acts as a buffer that compensates for delays and discrepancies in the transmission of quantum information.

problem_domains.problem: Logistical challenges and inventory management in grocery retail
problem_domains.description: The paper describes Save-On-Foods’ difficulty optimizing complex in-store logistics and inventory management across many constraints, which stretched classical computing to its limits.
problem_domains.quote: Save-On-Foods, a leading Canadian grocery chain, has successfully implemented quantum computing to tackle logistical challenges and enhance customer service. By partnering with D-Wave Systems, the company optimized grocery inventory management, reducing task processing time from 25 h to just two minutes.

problem_domains.problem: Complex logistical planning and restocking optimization
problem_domains.description: Save-On-Foods faced combinatorial complexity in optimizing restocking schedules and product assortments for each store, considering delivery windows, shelf life, promotions, and local preferences.
problem_domains.quote: Traditional algorithms struggled with the combinatorial complexity of optimizing grocery operations—for instance, determining the optimal restocking schedule and product assortment for each store while accounting for supplier delivery windows, shelf life, promotional events, and individual store consumer preferences.

problem_domains.problem: Enhancing customer service and product availability in retail
problem_domains.description: The retailer sought to improve product availability, reduce stockouts, and better meet consumer preferences to enhance the shopping experience.
problem_domains.quote: This quantum-driven approach has signiﬁcantly improved product availability, reduced stockouts, and ensured that consumer preferences are met efﬁciently, leading to a more satis- fying shopping experience.

problem_domains.problem: Traffic congestion and urban transportation efficiency
problem_domains.description: Volkswagen addressed the problem of traffic congestion and inefficient public transport flows during a large event, aiming to improve transportation experiences for consumers.
problem_domains.quote: Volkswagen has applied quantum computing to opti- mize trafﬁc ﬂow, improving transportation experiences for consumers. During the Web Summit conference in Lisbon, Volkswagen partnered with D-Wave to develop a quantum algorithm that reduced trafﬁc congestion, ensuring smoother and more efﬁcient public transport.

problem_domains.problem: Limits of traditional computing for real-time, large-scale consumer data analysis
problem_domains.description: The chapter frames a general problem where traditional computing and even advanced analytics struggle to process and analyze vast, complex consumer datasets in real time.
problem_domains.quote: Traditional computing methods, even with advanced analytics and machine learning, struggle to process and analyze these vast, complex datasets in real time.

problem_domains.problem: Capturing dynamic, context-dependent consumer decision behavior
problem_domains.description: Classical consumer decision models based on conventional probability theory falter when dealing with dynamic, context-dependent human choices.
problem_domains.quote: Classical consumer decision models rely on conventional probability theory and often assume relatively stable preferences and linear decision processes. These models can falter when addressing the dynamic, context-dependent nature of real human choices.

problem_domains.problem: Customer segmentation and real-time personalization under combinatorial complexity
problem_domains.description: Marketing applications such as evaluating all possible customer segment combinations and performing real-time personalization with many variables are constrained by classical computational limits.
problem_domains.quote: Early explorations in “quantum-enhanced marketing” suggest gains in customer segmentation, where all possible segment combinations might be evaluated in parallel [ 6], and in real-time personalization involving many variables simultaneously [4].

problem_domains.problem: Supply chain and retail operations optimization to improve customer experience
problem_domains.description: The chapter highlights the need to optimize supply chains and retail operations to reduce stockouts and better meet customer demand as a strategic marketing and operations problem.
problem_domains.quote: By integrating quantum computing into consumer behavior analysis, businesses can gain deeper insights into purchasing patterns, enhance personalization, and optimize supply chains.

problem_domains.problem: grocery logistics challenge / inventory management efficiency
problem_domains.description: Optimizing grocery logistics and inventory management, including restocking schedules, stockout reduction, and waste minimization under many interacting constraints.
problem_domains.quote: encoding the grocery logistics challenge (with variables representing, say, whether to reorder a product now or later, how to schedule staff for restocking, etc.) into a mathematical form that the quantum annealer could process.

problem_domains.description: Improving inventory management efficiency by reducing computation time for optimization, enabling more frequent re-optimization to reduce stockouts and overstocking.
problem_domains.quote: The immediate impact of the quantum pilot was a signiﬁcant improvement in inven- tory management efﬁciency. By reducing a 25-h computation to seconds, Save- On-Foods could re-run its optimization much more frequently and react faster to changes.
problem_domains.location: Section 3.3 Impact on Inventory Management, Page 267-268

problem_domains.problem: stockouts and overstocking / spoilage in perishables
problem_domains.description: Balancing inventory to avoid both stockouts and overstocking that leads to waste, especially for perishable goods.
problem_domains.quote: Store managers reported that product availability improved—shelves were replenished in a timelier manner, and instances of stockouts (products running out) were reduced, especially for high-demand items [9]. ... Additionally, the optimization likely balanced inventory levels to avoid overstocking, which can lead to waste (especially in perishables).
problem_domains.location: Section 3.3 Impact on Inventory Management, Page 267-268

problem_domains.description: Extending optimization beyond stores to warehouse management and distribution routing across the enterprise.
problem_domains.quote: This implies potential for scaling the solu- tion to all stores and extending it to other logistical challenges, such as warehouse management and distribution routing.
problem_domains.location: Section 3.3 Impact on Inventory Management, Page 268

problem_domains.problem: personalized marketing and loyalty programs / mass personalization
problem_domains.description: Using detailed customer and loyalty data to tailor inventory, assortments, and offers at the store or individual level, enabling mass personalization and micro-segmentation.
problem_domains.quote: A quantum algorithm can handle this additional layer of complexity by adjusting that store’s inventory and assort- ment to cater to this local preference, effectively enabling micro-segmentation at the store level. ... In marketing theory terms, this is mass personalization: each store (or even each customer) gets a tailored offering.
problem_domains.location: Section 3.4 Personalized Marketing and Loyalty Programs, Page 268-269

problem_domains.problem: optimal personalized offers and loyalty rewards / customer lifetime value
problem_domains.description: Finding optimal individualized rewards or discounts for each customer to maximize customer lifetime value and engagement.
problem_domains.quote: Quantum computing’s capacity to analyze “exponentially larger datasets” and identify complex patterns means it could, for instance, compute optimal personalized offers for thousands of customers simultaneously [ 5]. Early research suggests that quantum-inspired loyalty programs could use these capabilities to maxi- mize customer lifetime value, by quickly ﬁnding the best reward or discount for each customer based on their entire purchase history and predicted behavior [ 5].
problem_domains.location: Section 3.4 Personalized Marketing and Loyalty Programs, Page 268-269

problem_domains.problem: matching customers to products for promotions
problem_domains.description: Solving a large matching problem between customers and products to send individualized offers that also respect inventory and stock-movement needs.
problem_domains.quote: For Save-On-Foods, this could manifest as sending individualized weekly offers to loyalty members that account for their preferences, inventory levels, and the need to move certain stock—a task that involves solving a huge matching problem between customers and products, which quantum algorithms are well-suited for.
problem_domains.location: Section 3.4 Personalized Marketing and Loyalty Programs, Page 268-269

problem_domains.problem: formulating business problems in quantum terms
problem_domains.description: Translating real-world grocery logistics and operations objectives and constraints into a quantum-amenable optimization model.
problem_domains.quote: One hurdle was the need to formulate the business problem in quantum terms. Grocery operations experts had to work closely with D-Wave’s quantum scien- tists to translate a real-world logistics puzzle into an optimization model that a quantum annealer could solve [ 10].
problem_domains.location: Section 3.5 Implementation Challenges and Resolution, Page 269-270

problem_domains.description: Ensuring that the quantum optimization solution integrates with existing planning and IT systems without disrupting operations.
problem_domains.quote: Another challenge was ensuring that the quantum solution could integrate with existing store systems. Save-On-Foods approached this by starting with a single-store pilot, running the quantum optimizer in parallel with conven- tional planning systems to validate results.
problem_domains.location: Section 3.5 Implementation Challenges and Resolution, Page 269-270

problem_domains.problem: delivery truck route optimization for online grocery orders
problem_domains.description: Optimizing delivery truck routes to minimize delivery times for online grocery customers.
problem_domains.quote: Beyond inventory, executives have hinted at other problem areas that could be next, for example: optimizing delivery truck routes for online grocery orders (to minimize delivery times for customers)

V olkswagen identiﬁed trafﬁc management as a domain where advanced computing could make a difference for consumers (in this case, drivers and commuters).

problem_domains.problem: global traffic flow optimization across multiple vehicles
problem_domains.description: Coordinating routes across multiple vehicles simultaneously to find better city-wide traffic flow solutions than local, incremental optimizations.
problem_domains.quote: VW’s data scientists hypothesized that a global optimization approach using quantum computing could ﬁnd better trafﬁc ﬂow solutions by coordinating routes across multiple vehicles simultaneously, something classical routing algorithms struggle with in real time.

problem_domains.description: Computing near real-time route adjustments for a fleet of shuttle buses based on live traffic data to minimize congestion and travel time.
problem_domains.quote: As the buses began their routes, the system continually collected liv e trafﬁc data (from sensors or GPS feeds across Lisbon) and sent it to the cloud, where a D-Wave quantum annealer computed optimized route adjustments for each bus in near real-time [11].

problem_domains.problem: Classical computing hitting the wall in processing speed and efficiency
problem_domains.description: The paper frames current digital marketing as constrained by classical computing’s inability to process rapidly growing data volumes efficiently, leading to slow decision-making and missed opportunities.
problem_domains.quote: But, as data volumes are taking a disruption, classical computing is hitting the wall in processing speed and efﬁciency [2]. Businesses are now faced with massive datasets generated through customer interactions, online behavior, and real-time engagement metrics. It is increasingly difﬁcult to extract actionable insights from the data using classical computing methods, leading to slow decision-making and missed opportunities [ 3].

problem_domains.problem: Real-time personalization from massive customer data
problem_domains.description: The paper highlights that huge volumes of customer data from multiple channels make real-time personalization difficult with traditional methods, resulting in slow responses and generic campaigns.
problem_domains.quote: Modern digital marketing relies heavily on the interpretation of data to deliver personalized experiences. However, the tremendous volumes of customer data from social media, e-commerce, and web interactions make real-time personalization daunting. Traditional computing methods process information sequentially, which limits the velocity and accuracy of customer intelligence, often leading to slow response times and one-size-ﬁts-all marketing campaigns [ 12].

problem_domains.problem: Limited effectiveness of traditional A/B testing and campaign optimization
problem_domains.description: The paper notes that conventional A/B testing can only handle a few variations at a time, limiting the ability to optimize complex, multi-variable marketing campaigns.
problem_domains.quote: This change in data processing would allow companies to move from traditional A/ B testing and implement multi-variable personalization strategies. Instead of testing a few marketing variations at a time, brands would be able to test thousands of different messages, images, and calls to action at once to determine the optimal combinations in real-time.

problem_domains.problem: Inefficient ad targeting and real-time bidding
problem_domains.description: The paper frames current ad targeting and RTB as limited in their ability to analyze complex consumer behavior and many parameters in real time, leading to wasteful ad placements.
problem_domains.quote: Quantum algorithms can potentially streamline ad targeting by deciphering intricate consumer behaviors in real-time. The old-style A/B testing of advertisement campaigns could become history as quantum computers test numerous variations in parallel and yield demanding insights into consumer behavior. With quantum-powered analysis, marketers can instantly view which ad variants work best with different customer segments.

problem_domains.problem: SEO struggling with sophisticated user intent and changing ranking signals
problem_domains.description: The paper states that traditional SEO methods cannot keep up with increasingly complex search intent and the vast, evolving set of ranking signals.
